transcript:
Meeting header - 2026-01-30 10:00 UTC - duration approx 47 mins; attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Karen (Lakemont CTO), Ravi (Lakemont Eng Lead), Sofia (Lakemont SRE)

Summary section present at top (auto): Maya: quick recap of last week, we tuned routing and added prefix caching - saw improvements on short context tokens - baseline is still lower on 99th for a subset - we'll discuss.

[00:00] Maya: okay hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice. we have about 45 minutes. quick roll call - Ethan from Redwood on the call and I'll run through the updated bench.
[00:12] Karen: hi Maya, hi Ethan, thanks. morning.
[00:15] Ravi: morning all. we just want to see the bench contrasts and understand the trade offs before we commit to dedicated.
[00:23] Ethan: cool, real quick context - last week we adjusted routing thresholds to prefer lower-latency variants for sub-128 token requests and enabled KV prefix cache on the common prompt set. we also dropped batch size from 24 to 12 for latency-critical lanes.
[00:37] Ravi: can you remind me which model variant you used for the bench? was it the quantized 8-bit?
[00:41] Ethan: yeah we used redwood-pegasus-13b-8q (note: SE said 13b-8q, transcript may show pegasis or peg-13b), but for fairness we used the same tokenization and a compatible quant config as your baseline where possible. small differences expected.
[00:56] Maya: i'll share the bench spreadsheet link after the call - includes per-route breakdowns - median, p95, p99, and tail breakdown for cold start vs warm.
[01:05] Karen: great. okay show us the highlights.
[01:09] Ethan: slide - median latency for the primary test set - Redwood 72 ms vs incumbent 95 ms, so median is about 23 ms better. the p95 is the interesting bit - Redwood 310 ms vs incumbent 270 ms - so at p95 incumbent is lower right now.
[01:28] Ravi: wait the p95 is higher for you? why is that happening, did batching cause spikes?
[01:33] Ethan: good call - it's mostly a routing cadence interaction where some bursts got routed to a higher-capacity but slightly higher-latency host under our autoscaler settings. we observed 2 bursts in the run that aligned with checkpointing on the node that caused KV cache misses - so p95 blips.
[01:48] Sofia: that sounds like a cache warm up issue. in production we have spikey bursts of 800 rps for 30s windows - will that blow up your p95?
[01:56] Ethan: depends - with prefix caching and sticky routing to warm hosts we can mitigate. the playbook we propose pins warm threads for the known front-door patterns, then falls back to cold nodes with a lower concurrency cap.
[02:10] Karen: so the routing fix you mentioned last week, did that materially change the cost per token? because our finance team wants cost parity or better.
[02:18] Maya: the cost delta is primarily from the dedupe on batch sizing and cache efficiency - median improvements lower total tokens served per request when combined with caching hits. we estimate unit cost is down about 12% on the test set vs incumbent, but that depends on hit rate.
[02:34] Ravi: can you show cost at different cache hit percentiles?
[02:38] Ethan: in the sheet we have expected cost at 50%, 75%, 90% cache hit. i'll flag the 50-75 as our realistic range for your workload based on the traces we saw.
[02:47] Maya: important note - the incumbent vendor is running a custom low-latency infra in region-east, their p95 advantage appears only for heavy-parallel short bursts. for conversational flows your median matters more.
[03:02] Karen: hmm. our product team cares a lot about the p95 since we need consistent snappy replies. is there a way for you to show a head to head test under our peak bursts?
[03:10] Maya: yes we can do a dedicated head-to-head. propose a 48-hour slot where we both run the exact same traffic traces against your incumbent endpoint and against Redwood Dedicated. we will capture medians, p95, p99, and cost.
[03:25] Ravi: sounds good. realtime constraint: we have VPC peering, KMS keys managed in our account, and a couple of internal proxies that add 7-12 ms. will that affect parity?
[03:36] Ethan: we'll record those network latencies during the run. the test harness supports running from your VPC if we set up a private tunnel or arrange a peered subnet for the dedicated slot.
[03:47] Sofia: for security we need SC2 type evidence - sorry, SOC2. also the audit logs for request IDs tied to KMS key ops - can you provide that?
[03:56] Maya: yes, we have SOC 2 attestation and an audit logs package. for the Private deployment we can integrate with your KMS; for Hosted we'll provide encrypted-at-rest and key management options documented. i'll attach the security pack.
[04:10] Karen: okay good. also curious about quantization - if you go from 8-bit to 4-bit will that change the p95 behaviour?
[04:16] Ethan: 4-bit can reduce CPU work per token and lower median latency on some hardware but it increases the chance of slight quality regressions unless we calibrate. p95 effect depends on how the kernel behaves under heavy concurrency; sometimes it creates more jitter for tail latency. we recommend a calibration run.
[04:33] Ravi: any chance the incumbent is optimized for your particular workload? they may have tuned their KV placement.
[04:37] Ethan: possible - we saw they optimized for short prompt prefixes heavily. our caching can match that pattern but we need the real traces to tune placement and warm hosts.
[04:46] Maya: practical ask - can Ravi push two traffic traces: one steady-state conversational, one spikey burst pattern? that will let us simulate both and run the dedicated slot tests.
[04:55] Ravi: yes will do. i'll mark in the drive.
[05:00] Karen: on SLOs, we need 99% under 350 ms for user-facing prompts. do you think you can meet that with routing adjustments?
[05:07] Ethan: given current bench numbers, with sticky warm routing and a small increase in reserved warm capacity we think we can get p99 under 350 for the majority of cases. the cost will go up a bit for reserved warm slots. we can quantify in the dedicated run.
[05:20] Sofia: do you have a fallback playbook if an entire AZ goes noisy? our app can't show long delays to clinicians.
[05:27] Maya: yes we have a fallback lane - policy routes to a lower-capacity but validated model variant in another region, with graceful degradation and a percent-based fallback. we also support A/B style canaries and automatic failover to the incumbent endpoint as a last resort.
[05:40] Ravi: how fast is that failover?
[05:42] Ethan: typical detection + failover is 10-30s depending on metrics, we can tune aggressive thresholds for clinical flows.
[05:49] Karen: ok that 10s is not ideal but better than user visible timeouts. can you add a health-check heartbeat at the front door so we can measure failover latency?
[05:57] Ethan: yes we'll add a synthetic heartbeat and surface it in the console dashboards.
[06:02] Maya: wrapping to next steps - we'll provision dedicated slot options and send a calendar poll, Ethan will prepare a routing + quantization doc, and Ravi will upload traces.
[06:12] Sofia: quick question - audit logs retention, how long are they kept for Hosted?
[06:16] Maya: default is 90 days but enterprise retention add-on can extend to 365 days. private on-prem deployments can match any retention you need.
[06:24] Karen: that's fine. thanks everyone. anything else?
[06:29] Ravi: just one more - does Redwood surface token-level cost per request in the console for us to tie to feature flags?
[06:36] Ethan: yes we have token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards; we'll show you a quick walkthrough in the next demo.
[06:43] Maya: cool. thanks all, i'll send the security pack and the pricing/dedicated-slot options after this call.
[06:49] Karen: thanks. bye.

End of transcript - total duration aligns to 47 minutes recorded. Notes: occasional mis-ids and filler words present.
